children: Meta Platforms Inc.
faced fresh scrutiny in Brazil over technical restrictions affecting President
Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
’s Instagram campaign account and the recommendation of challenger
Flavio Bolsonaro
’s accounts, days before the Oct. 25 presidential runoff.
Meta employees acknowledged in internal messages that the restrictions hindered Lula’s accounts during the election, Folha de S.Paulo reported on Friday, citing messages it reviewed.
Meta Denies Political Bias
According to the report, the messages also said the platform recommended the profile and WhatsApp channel of challenger Senator
Flavio Bolsonaro
Meta said the technical issues cited in the report were already public. It said the conversations concerned their severity, not political interference.
"Any suggestion that Meta favors one side is false," the company said in a statement to Reuters.
Regulatory Risk Builds for Meta Ahead of Runoff

Earlier this week, Lula’s party said it would file a complaint with the Organization of American States, alleging Meta manipulated social media during the election. It said some posts lacked a share button or had reduced reach.

On Thursday, a justice at Brazil’s top electoral court ordered Meta not to unjustifiably limit the reach of political content tied to either candidate through the end of the runoff campaign. The ruling also bars Meta AI, its chatbot, from favoring either candidate.
Lula faces Bolsonaro in the runoff after the senator outperformed expectations in the first round.
Trading Metrics
Meta has a market capitalization of $1.81 trillion, a 52-week high of $779.82 and a 52-week low of $520.26.
Over the past 12 months, the large-cap stock has fallen 0.39%.
